newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ futures end up slightly in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ futures end up slightly in thin trade.

text.p: Frozen concentrated orange juice futures ended barely firmer as prices continued to stabilize after a sharp decline earlier this month, analysts said.
The market awaits a tree census by the U.S. Department of Agriculture released today, on which Florida crop estimates are based. The USDA will release its next crop production report in a month.
Dull activity is expected ahead of the report. Today, volume was estimated at a mere 1,200 lots.

Expections for the Florida crop hover around 215 million 90-lb boxes. "The lower prices would suggust the market has discounted a figure in excess of 215 million boxes," said Merrill Lynch analyst Judith Ganes. "Should the estimate come in lower, the market is likely to spring higher from here."
November FCOJ settled up 0.55 cent a lb at 106.55, having ranged from 107.20 to 106.00. The remaining months closed 0.70 higher to 0.90 lower.
Meantime, the market dismissed news of a reduction in a Brazilian tax, which could encourage additional sales in the U.S., Ganes noted.
Support basis the most-active November remained at the recent low of 103.00 reached Sept 5. Resistance was seen between 110.00 and 112.00.
